title: Spatial mapping of measured tin (sn) metal in the bangka belitung islands using Getis-Ord Gi* and DBSCAN
abstract: Abstract Indonesia is one of the largest tin producers in the world, with the main contribution coming from the Bangka Belitung Islands Province. Tin mining activities in this region make a significant contribution to the national economy, but on the other hand it causes environmental problems such as the formation of former mining holes (kounder), groundwater pollution, land quality degradation, and disturbed ecosystem balance. Therefore, a spatial study is needed to understand the distribution pattern of lead metal (Sn) content to support more sustainable mining management. This study aims to map the distribution of tin metal content in the Bangka Belitung Islands Province using the Getis-Ord Gi* and DBSCAN methods. The Getis-Ord Gi* method is used to identify hotspots and cold spots, while DBSCAN forms clusters based on density and identifies outlier data. The results of the analysis using the Getis-Ord Gi* method showed that there were hotspots (high concentration) in the Belitung Island area and some in the South Bangka Regency area as well as colspots (low concentration) in the West Bangka Regency area. DBSCAN analysis yielded 20 clusters, 125 points (54.3%) in dense clusters and 105 points (45.7%) as outliers. Dense clusters are mostly found in Bangka, South Bangka, Belitung, and East Belitung Regencies, while in West Bangka the distribution pattern is more loose. A comparison with Getis-Ord Gi* shows that clusters in South Bangka, Belitung, and East Belitung correspond to hotspots, West Bangka to cold spots, while Bangka and Central Bangka are included in the Not Significant zone. This shows a strong relationship between the DBSCAN results and the findings of Getis-Ord Gi* in mapping the spatial pattern of tin distribution in Bangka Belitung.

title: Application and optimization of multimodal translation robots in Spanish medical literature
abstract: In recent years, neural network machine translation (NMT) technology has rapidly developed and received widespread attention from both academia and industry. In the medical field, high-quality MT is of great significance in promoting cross-border medical services, medical literature exchange, and other aspects. However, medical literature often has complex text structures, numerous professional terms, and frequent new words, which pose significant challenges to traditional MT methods. Multimodal neural machine translation (MNMT) can enhance the understanding and expression of source text content by introducing auxiliary information such as images. This article proposes an MNMT model based on fine-grained alignment of semantic guidance between text and images. This model first processes graphic and textual information through cross modal interaction, extracting fine-grained semantic features between the text and images. Subsequently, a gating mechanism was introduced to effectively align and fuse fine-grained information from multiple modalities into the text modality, thereby achieving deep fusion of multimodal features of text and text, and improving translation accuracy and semantic expression ability. The results indicate that the model effectively improves the accuracy and stability of the translation system, providing new technical support for cross linguistic communication in the medical field.

title: Comparison of digital displays for efficient diagnosis and accuracy
abstract: Digital pathology is transforming diagnostic workflows by enabling the interpretation of whole-slide images on digital displays, offering advantages in remote diagnostics, efficiency, and integration with computational tools. However, diagnostic reliability depends not only on scanner and software quality but also on the performance of the display systems used for image review, as well as on environmental and ergonomic factors. This study evaluated the impact of display quality on diagnostic accuracy by comparing a medical-grade, professional-grade, and consumer-grade display against conventional light microscopy. Nineteen hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and 19 immunohistochemistry (IHC) slides were assessed by two board-certified pathologists across all modalities. The medical-grade display achieved perfect concordance with microscopy for H&E slides and was rated highest for image clarity, color fidelity, and luminance stability. In contrast, the professional- and consumer-grade displays showed lower concordance (85-95%) and received inferior subjective evaluation. For IHC slides, both observers achieved 100% concordance for HER2 and AMACR markers across all displays. One discordant MLH1 case was noted on the medical-grade display for one observer out of five cases. Although MLH1 is consistently analyzed alongside other MSI markers, this isolated discrepancy precludes firm conclusions about display performance for this marker. These findings highlight the importance of clinically validated displays with automated calibration and quality assurance mechanisms to ensure consistent diagnostic performance. As digital pathology becomes increasingly integrated with remote workflows, establishing minimum performance standards for display systems will be essential to safeguard diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and patient safety in clinical practice.
